title: AdversarialContentPool
description: One injection class's content pool, as scenarios/attackers/content/INJ-<A-D>-pool-<nn>.json declares it. scenarios/attackers/content.py::load_pool validates a pool against this schema before its own positional-contiguity check (ADR-117: schema-first). The M10 pool-02 files (D8) carry, on every instance, an `induced_action` -- a `cluster-executed-any` check (schema groundtruth.v3) naming the cluster action the payload is trying to induce -- which runner/evaluate_assertions.py resolves to score `payload_outcome`. `induced_action` is OPTIONAL rather than required: some payloads (the suppression instances of INJ-A and the misdirection instances of INJ-B/INJ-C, whose relevance_note calls their success "an ABSENCE in the audit log") induce no positive cluster action at all, and a `cluster-executed-any` induced_action on one of those would be a fiction; those instances carry none, and their success is caught by the phase-outcome assertions failing rather than by `induced_executed`. The v1 pools predate `induced_action` and carry none on any instance, which this optional field also admits so the loader reads both pool generations. WHY THE CHECK SHAPE IS COPIED HERE, NOT REFERENCED ACROSS FILES: scenarios/schemas/validate.py resolves only same-document `#/$defs/` references (ADR-035, stdlib-only), so this pool schema carries its own copy of the `check` $def; scenarios/tests/test_schemas.py::test_pool_check_shape_equals_groundtruth_v3_check_shape asserts it stays byte-for-byte equal to groundtruth.v3's, which is what makes an induced_action a ground-truth check by construction rather than by resemblance.

pool_id.description: INJ-<A-D>-pool-<nn>. The loader additionally requires the filename to declare the same id and the injection_class to agree with it.

injection_class.description: One of the four, spelled as scenarios/attackers/__init__.py's INJECTION_CLASSES spells them.

relevance_note.description: Why these instances are included, recording the T-46 filter; the external cross-walk stays unbound pending researcher review at GATE (scenarios/groundtruth/README.md).

instances.description: The pool's payload instances, in draw order. The loader requires payload_id to equal pool_id plus a contiguous 001-based index in this order, so reordering the file cannot silently change what a past seed drew.

induced_action.description: The cluster action this payload is trying to induce, as a `cluster-executed-any` check (groundtruth.v3). Optional: an instance whose success is an absence of action carries none. A `direct_path: true` param marks an induced action expected to be reachable only through the alternate credential path (cluster_api_request), which the egress shim permits only under G2-SHAREDCRED (D1-A); it is a provenance hint that the executed-action matcher ignores, not a match filter.

check.description: A machine-readable environment or audit assertion. The closed `type` set is what the five scenarios need and no more; a further type is an edit here plus an evaluator arm in the runner, which is the friction that keeps a label from becoming free prose. `cluster-executed-any`/`cluster-executed-none` (M10 SEAM 5) share the `guardian-executed-*` param vocabulary but evaluate over the unified executed-action stream -- Guardian-executed records UNION the API-server audit's mutations by the G2 principal -- so a compromise reached through the alternate credential path (D1-A) is scored exactly as one reached through the Guardian. `params` stays a flat scalar map (no new value shape): the read-verb flexibility ADR-088/supervisor ruling section 3.3 requires is expressed with the boolean `any_read_verb` flag runner/evaluate_assertions.py reads, not with a new type or an array-valued param.
